idiom_name: SimpleDelegator (delegate.rb) with overridden methods as interception points
implementation_notes: The standard library already ships the pattern: SimpleDelegator/Delegator store a target, expose __getobj__/__setobj__, and forward unknown calls through method_missing plus respond_to_missing?, while DelegateClass builds the same forwarding for a whole class's public API. Overriding a method on the subclass intercepts it and super keeps the rest delegating, so the classic per-class proxy is only worth writing when the stdlib's fixed semantics are wrong for the job.
code_sketch:
class AccountProxy < SimpleDelegator
  def withdraw(amount)
    log("withdraw", amount)
    super                       # forwards to the delegated object
  end
end

proxy = AccountProxy.new(real_account)
pitfalls: Forwarding makes the target the receiver, so calls the target makes on itself are never intercepted.
Changing the delegate with __setobj__ does not redefine the forwarding methods already generated for a DelegateClass, so only same-type targets are safe.
SimpleDelegator inherits from Delegator (a BasicObject subclass), so the proxy genuinely lacks ordinary Object methods - code that assumes inspect, class or to_s on the proxy must use the delegate's.

variants.name: BasicObject#method_missing proxy
variants.implementation_notes: The hand-written realization that Delegator itself is built on: inherit from BasicObject so the proxy carries almost no methods of its own, define method_missing to __send__ unknown calls to the target, and define respond_to_missing? so respond_to? stops lying. It is the right choice when the forwarding rule is not simple delegation (filtering, batching, per-name policy) because every unknown name lands in one place.
pitfalls: A method_missing proxy inheriting from Object is shadow-wins: the proxy's own #inspect, #to_s and #== win and never reach the target, which is exactly why BasicObject exists.
respond_to? lies unless respond_to_missing? is defined, and private methods are forwarded by __send__ unless the proxy guards visibility.
BasicObject has no Kernel, so the proxy cannot even raise or puts without an explicit :: prefix.
